name: Precision Grid
tagline: A Swiss-modern recipe index where measurement becomes the luxury cue.
thesis: Paul's Cookbook is redesigned as a disciplined cooking reference: visible modular structure, hairline strata, clean photography, and tabular prep/price numerals that make the collection feel precise without becoming cold.

typography.display: DIN Condensed / Arial Narrow / Aptos Display for a Swiss annual headline cadence without external font dependencies
typography.ui: Aptos / Helvetica Neue / Arial / system UI for precise bilingual controls
typography.data: JetBrains Mono/SFMono/Consolas for tabular minutes, counts, and RON values
typography.scale: 16px body minimum, 20px+ section heads, 13px+ metadata, large mode at 112.5%

moves: Exactly two recipe columns through 640px, then denser 3/4-column reference grids above.
Category sections are indexed strata: rule, 01-08 numeral, label, and right-aligned live count.
Recipe cards remove overlays and shadows; photography is a plain rectangle and the data line carries status.
Prep minutes and price per serving are aligned mono numerals with quiet units and explicit partial/unavailable states.
The control strip behaves like an instrument panel with count, active filters, grouping, and field+direction sort state.
The drawer preserves filters, categories, more links, and preferences as a numbered systematic index.
tradeoffs: The design is intentionally austere; warmth comes from real food photography rather than decorative illustration.
Four columns on desktop prioritize reference scanning over large editorial imagery.
No webfont dependency is used, so the concept degrades through local serif/sans/mono stacks.
